::: {#def-positional-invariance .theorem}
# Positional invariance

We say component functions $g_{ti}$ are positionally invariant if for $i,j \in \mathscr{N}$, $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{X}' \in \{0,1\}^n$ and conformable permutation matrix $\mathbf{M}$:

$$
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{X}_{\mathscr{N}_i} = \mathbf{M} \mathbf{X'}_{\mathscr{N}_j} \text{ and } \Psi_{i\mathscr{N}_i} =  \mathbf{M} \Psi_{j\mathscr{N}_j}\\
\implies \\
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}) = g_{tj}(\mathbf{X'}) 
\end{equation}
$$
:::
